title: CSS Introduction
summary: CSS changes the look of a web page. Try a colour, a text size and a border, one small rule at a time.
introduction: Imagine that HTML makes a plain school poster. CSS is the art kit that gives it colours, sizes and space. You write a rule to tell the browser what to change. In this lesson, you will make a heading blue and give a box a border.
learningObjectives: Explain what CSS changes on a page
Read a CSS rule one part at a time
Change a colour and add space inside a box

blocks.text: **CSS** stands for Cascading Style Sheets. A style is a choice about how something looks. HTML says, "This is a heading." CSS says, "Make that heading blue." CSS can change the look of a button, but it does not decide what to do when someone clicks it.

items: `h1` chooses the main heading. This part is called the **selector**.
`{` and `}` hold the choices for that heading.
`color` is the **property**: the thing to change.
`blue` is the **value**: the choice we want.
The colon `:` joins the property to its value. The semicolon `;` ends that choice.

blocks.text: `font-size` changes the size of the letters. `px` means pixels, a unit used to measure things on a screen. Try `24px`, then `40px`. What changes?
Step 3: Give a box some space

The sample page has a box with `class="card"`. The dot in `.card` chooses things with that class name. A `border` is a line around a box. `padding` is the space between that line and the words inside it.

rows: Chooses which page parts to style, such as `h1` or `.card`.
The thing you change, such as `color`.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Write the punctuation too. `color: blue;` has a colon and a semicolon. Put the choices inside `{ }`. One missing mark can stop a rule from working.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Change blue to green in one example. Run it. Next, change the card padding from `16px` to `32px`. Does the space inside the border grow?

seo.title: CSS Introduction – What CSS Is and Your First Stylesheet
seo.description: Learn what CSS is for, what it leaves to HTML and JavaScript, how browsers apply rules to elements, and write your first stylesheet with a live result.
